messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident fired: PD#INC-4129 — capacity_pressure in 'inference-cell-7' (queue backlog > 90%). Auto-escalation policy: page primary oncall. See https://pd.example/INC-4129

pagerduty: Incident INC-4129 acknowledged by sam

sam: Acking — I'm on it. Quick check: is this KV cache pressure or pure worker shortage?

ria: initial graphs show active queue depth spiking from 120 -> 3.4k over 6m, CPU on serving nodes ~40% but GPUs saturated (95%). Autoscaler attempted 3 adds but failed with quota errors: "node quota exceeded" in cloud-provider logs.

mike: confirmed. GCP quota caps for GPUs in region are hit. Autoscaler retries but backoff prevents rapid recovery.

julia: customer impact: a handful of real-time inference customers seeing 500/timeout errors and elevated latencies (>5s). ALB error-rate up 6% in last 10m. No widespread data loss.

sam: ok, mitigation options: 1) manual emergency scale to dedicated spare pool (if available), 2) route new requests to warm fallback model in other region, 3) throttle non-critical routes. Trying 2 and 3 now.

ops-sre: running kube patch to set route policy for low-priority routes -> degrade. Command: `kubectl -n inference patch cm routing-config -p '{"data":{"priority":"degrade"}}'` — applying.

mike: starting cross-region failover for chat-low-critical. Using runbook step 4. PD runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/autoscale-kvcell

julia: notifying CS about partial degradation for customers with live inference. Drafting message now.

sam: manual scale: requesting quota bump is slow; we're going to spin up nodes from dedicated spare capacity pool. Running: `infractl allocate --pool spare-gpu-pool --count 6 --reason "INC-4129"`

incident-bot: infractl job started: job-9832. ETA nodes 2m-4m.

ria: logs from autoscaler: `ERROR: nodeGroupCreate failed: quotaExceeded: compute.googleapis.com/accelerator-p100 count` — confirms GPU quota. Also saw repeated 429s to cloud API.

mike: while we wait, enabling local KV cache eviction to free memory and reduce per-request cost. Running `kubectl exec -it kvcache-0 -- /opt/bin/evict-prefixes --age=300`

julia: CS message sent to impacted customers: short note + mitigation in progress. Link to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-4129

sam: job-9832 reports nodes registered: 4/6 (2m). Starting scale-up of serving replicas.

ops-sre: scaling command: `kubectl scale deployment inference-serving --replicas=120 -n inference` — pods coming up, but readiness probe failing on 3 due to image pull rate limit. Pull throttle from registry causing delays.

ria: swapping to pre-pulled image set on spare pool. Patch applied. New pods becoming ready.

pagerduty: INC-4129 status: acknowledged by sam; responders: sam, ria, mike; escalation disabled for now.

mike: traffic shift in progress: new requests diverted to inference-cell-2 (us-west-2) for low-priority routes. Running gradual 10% steps. Monitor errors.

julia: CS updated customers: degraded performance and partial timeouts mitigated by cross-region routing. Customers asked to report if issues persist.

sam: latency trending down from 4.8s -> 1.2s for degraded route after 8m. Error rate dropping but still above baseline for some tenants.

ops-sre: autoscaler still reporting failed attempts for new node groups due to quota; opened cloud support ticket 123456. Requested temporary quota raise.

ria: root-cause candidate: sudden spike from a batch of heavy-generative workloads plus an internal load-test that hit production routing unexpectedly (investigating tagging and recent deploys).

mike: action items: 1) keep spare pool allocation until baseline stable, 2) lock down routing for internal load-tests, 3) follow up with infra to request permanent quota increase or add overflow capacity.

julia: I'll create post-incident customer summary once incident is closed.

sam: handing off to night oncall — @ops-sre you take next watch. I'll update PD: change responder to ops-sre and set note.

pagerduty: INC-4129 reassigned to ops-sre by sam

ops-sre: taking over. Current status: backlog draining, consumer error-rate 1.2% above baseline, nodes stable. I'll monitor for 1h and close if steady.

incident-bot: Reminder: create incident postmortem and link PR for runbook updates.

sam: thanks team. leaving notes in the incident doc.
